manual:
*Legality flag:* the famous Stein OTK targets (`Cyber Twin Dragon`, `Cyber End Dragon`) are **post-TLM and illegal**. The GOAT-legal kill uses `Master of Oz` + `Megamorph`; `Cyber-Stein` is Limited (1) so this is a *backup* inside a control shell.

**Game plan:** play straight Goat Control until you can assemble the one-card burst kill.

**Key cards / engine:** Cyber-Stein → Master of Oz → Megamorph.

**How to pilot / combo lines:**
- **The math (all [CDB]):** `Cyber-Stein` "pay 5000 LP; Special Summon 1 Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck in Attack Position" → summon `Master of Oz` (4200 ATK). You are now at **3000 LP**. `Megamorph`: "While your LP is lower than your opponent's, the equipped monster's ATK becomes double its original ATK" → 4200 × 2 = **8400**, exactly lethal through an open board.
- **Set it up:** clear blockers first with `Brain Control`/`Snatch Steal` (steal their monster, swing or tribute it) so Master of Oz connects; revive a used `Cyber-Stein` with `Premature Burial`/`Call of the Haunted` for a second attempt.
- Until you draw the pieces, pilot Goat Control: Scapegoat→TER, Tsukuyomi value, full trap suite.

**Weaknesses:** you dip to 3000 LP mid-combo, so a live `Ring of Destruction`/`Sakuretsu`/`Mirror Force` can kill or blank you — only commit when it ends the game; `Megamorph` and Master of Oz are otherwise dead draws.

=== EXTRA DECK ===

**Two doors: `Cyber-Stein` for the kill, `Metamorphosis` — "Tribute 1 monster. Special Summon 1 Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck with the same Level as the Tributed monster" [CDB] for everything else.** No `Polymerization`; `Magical Scientist` is **Forbidden** in GOAT [GF-BAN]. Tokens are legal material ("including a Sheep Token from `Scapegoat`"), Metamorphosis "cannot be activated" if no Fusion in the list matches the tributed monster's Level, and it "does not properly Summon a Fusion Monster, so you cannot use `Monster Reborn` on it afterwards" [GR].

**Fodder by Level — Lv1:** Sheep Token, `Sinister Serpent`, `Magician of Faith`. **Lv5:** `Airknight Parshath`. **Lv6:** `Chaos Sorcerer`. **Lv9:** nothing — Stein only.

- **`Master of Oz` (Lv9) is the payload, and Stein is its only door:** "With 4200 attack and 3700 defense, this has the best stats of any fusion monster in Goat Format. You won't be summoning it with Metamorphosis too often, but it is a common Cyber-Stein target" [GF-FUS]. The sourced OTK is this deck's plan verbatim: "by paying 5000 life points, the Stein pilot can summon Master of Oz and power it up" with `Megamorph` [GF-STEIN]. ⚠ Real Stein lists lean on `Giant Trunade` — named "the third combo piece" — plus `Enemy Controller` to make the lethal swing connect [GF-STEIN]; this shell substitutes `Brain Control` and `Snatch Steal`, so budget the removal *before* you pay the 5000.
- **`Thousand-Eyes Restrict` (Lv1) is what you do while you wait for the pieces:** "the most frequent and most powerful fusion monster special summoned with Metamorphosis … it can take the opponent's best monster while locking down the field at the same time" [GF-FUS]. Goats in their End Phase [GW], token → Metamorphosis on your turn, then **absorb with priority** — in GOAT rules "when a Chain or Summon has finished resolving, the turn player can activate a fast effect *or a monster's Ignition Effect* before the opponent is allowed to respond" [GF-BASICS], so equip the instant Metamorphosis resolves, before `Book of Moon` can land; if they flip it down first, TER "needs to be face up on the field to attach a monster to itself, so its effect will fizzle" [GR]. `Tsukuyomi` ×2 flips TER down and back up for a second absorb — "when combined with Tsukuyomi, Restrict can take full control of the board and chip in for damage until the game is won" [GF-GOAT]. Also, monsters equipped to TER "do not have effects and are treated as Equip Spell Cards" [GR], so it blanks what it steals.
- **`Dark Balter the Terrible` (Lv5) off a spent `Airknight Parshath`** [GW] — "after Thousand-Eyes Restrict, this is the most commonly used fusion monster brought forth with Metamorphosis … the potential to negate both spells and monster effects is quite powerful" [GF-FUS]: it pays 1000 LP to negate a Normal Spell (`Pot of Greed`, `Graceful Charity`, `Heavy Storm`, `Nobleman of Crossout`) and negates the effect of any Effect Monster it kills in battle [CDB]. In this deck it doubles as combo insurance: it is your only way to stop the opposing `Heavy Storm` that would otherwise strip your board before the Stein turn.
- **`Ryu Senshi` (Lv6) off `Chaos Sorcerer`**, "the most commonly used level 6 fusion monster, and it [is] mostly used for setting up kill turns via Chaos Sorcerer+Metamorphosis" [GF-FUS]. It pays 1000 LP to negate a **Normal Trap** (`Mirror Force`, `Torrential Tribute`, `Sakuretsu Armor`, `Ring of Destruction` — *not* the Counter Trap `Solemn Judgment`) and "negate[s] the effects of any Spell Card that targets this card and destroy[s] it" [CDB], walking through `Book of Moon` and `Snatch Steal`. ⚠ Note it protects *itself*, not your `Cyber-Stein` — it is a second, slower clock, not combo protection.
- **`Musician King` (Lv5) — the LIGHT slot, for Chaos, not a body.** 1750 vanilla; the sourced use of a LIGHT Level-5 Fusion is graveyard fuel: "in the rare situations where you have `Snatch Steal` for your opponent's `Airknight Parshath` and need to Metamorphosis for a light monster in your graveyard for a chaos monster [it] could be the difference between winning and losing the game" [GF-FUS]. The stolen monster goes back to *their* Graveyard when tributed, so the LIGHT you bank is the Fusion when it dies, re-arming `Chaos Sorcerer`/`BLS` ("1 LIGHT and 1 DARK" banished [CDB]). That guide picks `Giltia the D. Knight` (also LIGHT, Level 5, 1850 ATK) for this slot and never names Musician King — same job, 100 more ATK.
